title: Romania Visa Information — Embassy of Romania in the Republic of Serbia

embassy_in_serbia.name: Embassy of Romania in the Republic of Serbia — Consular Section
embassy_in_serbia.address: Mihaila Avramovica 12, 11040 Belgrade, Serbia (Entry B for Consular Section)

visa_eligibility.serbian_citizens: Serbian citizens do NOT require a visa for stays in Romania up to 90 days within any 180-day period. For stays exceeding 90 days (long-stay, D-type visas), Serbian citizens must apply online at eviza.mae.ro and then attend an in-person appointment at the Consular Section. Short-stay C visas are only needed by Serbian citizens in exceptional circumstances beyond the 90-day limit.
visa_eligibility.other_nationals: Third-country nationals holding a valid permit for temporary or permanent residence in Serbia may also submit visa applications at the Consular Section of the Romanian Embassy in Belgrade.

processing_times.notes: Short-stay C visa: standard approval within 10–15 business days; invitation approval (if required) up to 60 days. Long-stay D visa (employment with permit): 10 days. Long-stay D visa (other categories, no permit): 30–45 days. Online appointment waiting time is typically 2–3 weeks, sometimes longer; this period does not count toward processing time. Apply within 30 days of invitation approval (if applicable).

application_location.center: Consular Section of the Embassy of Romania in Belgrade
application_location.booking: Applications must first be pre-registered electronically at https://eviza.mae.ro/ for pre-validation and to obtain an appointment. In-person attendance at the Consular Section is then mandatory.

visa_fees.service_fee: Standard C-visa fee is €60; however, Serbian nationals benefit from the EU–Serbia Visa Facilitation Agreement, which reduces the fee to €35. Certain categories are fully exempt (see fee_exemptions). Long-stay D-visa fee not separately published; confirm with embassy.
fee_exemptions: School pupils, students, postgraduate students, and accompanying teachers travelling for study or educational purposes
Disabled persons and, where necessary, their accompanying persons
Close relatives of Serbian citizens legally residing in Romania (spouses, children under 21, dependent ascendants)
Holders of diplomatic and service passports
Participants in official exchange programmes of twin towns

required_documents_all_applicants: Completed and signed harmonised visa application form
Recent passport-style photograph (3.5 × 4.5 cm, white background, taken within last 6 months)
Valid travel document (passport issued within the last 10 years, valid at least 3 months after intended exit from Romania, with at least 2 blank pages)
Travel/health insurance covering at least €30,000 for medical expenses, emergency repatriation, and urgent care, valid for the entire stay
Proof of financial means: minimum €50 per day, with at least €500 for the total stay (bank statements, credit card with statement not older than 2 days, or sponsorship declaration)
Proof of accommodation (hotel reservation, notarised invitation letter from host, or property ownership documents)
Proof of return/onward transportation (air, rail, or bus ticket; or vehicle registration, driver's licence, and Romanian vignette if travelling by car)
additional_documents_by_nationality: Third-country nationals resident in Serbia must present a valid Serbian residence permit (temporary or permanent) when applying at the Belgrade Consular Section

required: Visa application form signed by both parents (or the person exercising permanent or temporary parental authority/guardianship)
Copy of both parents' passports or identity documents
Notarised parental consent letter from the non-accompanying parent (or both, if the minor travels alone)
Court decision or sole-custody documentation if only one parent has parental authority
For unaccompanied minors: notarised authorisation identifying the accompanying person
documents_for_minors.note: For minors applying for long-stay D visas, additional purpose-specific documents are required (e.g., school enrolment letter for study visas).

tourism: Confirmed hotel reservation or accommodation voucher for entire stay
Round-trip travel itinerary or travel agency booking confirmation
Proof of financial means covering the stay (€50/day minimum)
business: Invitation letter from the Romanian company or business partner specifying purpose, duration, and financial responsibility
Company registration extract or official letterhead of the inviting Romanian entity
Applicant's employment contract or business registration document
family_or_private_visit: Notarised invitation letter from the host in Romania (Romanian national or legal resident) specifying relationship, duration, and accommodation
Host's proof of residence in Romania (ID, utility bill, or residence certificate)
Proof of relationship between applicant and host (e.g., birth certificate, marriage certificate)
Proof of host's financial means if sponsoring the applicant
medical_treatment: Letter from a Romanian medical institution confirming appointment, treatment type, and estimated duration
Proof of payment or financial guarantee for medical treatment
Referral letter from treating physician in Serbia (if applicable)
Proof of financial means covering medical and living costs
transit: Valid visa or residence permit for the destination country (if required)
Confirmed onward travel booking (flight, rail, or bus ticket)
Proof of sufficient financial means for transit stay

employees: Employment certificate from employer (stating position, salary, leave approval, and confirmation of return)
entrepreneurs: Tax returns or financial statements for the last year
students: Enrolment certificate from educational institution in Serbia
Proof of scholarship or financial support
Letter from institution confirming leave of absence (if applicable)
For long-stay study D visa: acceptance/enrolment letter from Romanian university or educational institution
retirees: Pension certificate or proof of pension income
Bank statements showing regular pension payments
Proof of sufficient financial means for stay

special_provisions: As of 1 September 2020, the Embassy in Belgrade processes Type D (long-stay) visa applications in addition to short-stay C visas. All applications must be pre-submitted electronically at https://eviza.mae.ro/ before an in-person appointment can be scheduled. Romania is a full EU member state but as of 2026 still operates its own national visa system (it joined Schengen for air and sea borders in March 2024; land border Schengen entry expected separately). Serbian citizens enjoy visa-free access for up to 90 days and are covered by the EU–Serbia Visa Facilitation Agreement for any C-visa applications required. ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) is expected to apply to non-EU nationals by late 2026; holders of a valid Romanian visa would be exempt from ETIAS.
